title: Drushei HaMalbush, Vol. 4: Map and Territory
subtitle: Pshat and sod, Alma and Oraita, and the kelim needed to wake from the dream.
html:
From Mikraei Kodesh, the Torah writings collected on liorsollyshachar.com.

סדר ב'

The chochmah begins with the following observation: Reality is at once one and many. We begin by seeing one thing, but chochmah is about learning to see something else. The perceived ‘many’ is not a true description of reality. Instead, we perceive the miraculous gilui of (n.) ‘Gvurot’. We will discover that we can have productive discussions assuming the virtual1 many that is given existence, despite the space of its existence in actuality being Echad.

With that in mind, we shift our gaze to Torah which turns out to be at once one and many, much like the world that issues therefrom. There is a system, composed of different parts, related as layers, named by the adjectives Pshat Remez Drush & Sod. Practically, we in the majority have primary exposure to chochmah in the region called Pshat2. I wonder how the contrast between these three higher dimensions and pshat materializes. Is the difference articulated within pshat, i.e., simply a new understanding of that same material we’ve learned? Or perhaps the space of the higher layers is populated by material of its own, not to be found in the bookshelves of pshat at all until you relearn pshat in light of that new material found elsewhere? And if we assume the latter, that there are different books containing the other layers, then we are saying pshat alone will not yield the picture contained in the three parallel dimensions (despite that they are parallel), and so we can point the question inward. There are kelim which we build in order to engage with pshat. Is sod differentiated from pshat merely in material, leaving us to use the same Gar3 with which we penetrate the chochmah of pshat? Or perhaps there is a new system of kelim without which we can’t even discuss that region of chochmah?

To reduce the obscurity, follow this logic: If kelim shape the Ohr, and Ohr Chohmah (i.e. Torah) is what makes any given reality (as in the Zohar Terumah ‘Istakal Beoraita Ubara Alma’), and we want to develop the kli for the particular Ohr Chochmah that generates the world of Sod, then we need our ratzon to take aim at the reality we are after rather than the chochmah as such. We need to want to make contact with vision of the Sod world, and we need to find out who we must be to enable that envisioning, as well as find out what material contains this vision.

Reality is the map that references the territory of Torah. Torah is the Ohr which En Sof Baruch Hu evidently decided to ma’atzil, but He is the reality. So really, He is reality, and made the Torah, which is a map of a particular universe that is an expression of Reality, but the universe that emanates from that Torah is a map that references the territory of Torah.

The following may seem philosophical at first but it is in fact a cornerstone of the chochmah and a bank vault of value that is rarely spoken out in the following way. The distinction employed is map vs territory. A map is not a territory, but it references the territory within its self-contained system of symbols. The first problematique of epistemology is not the construction of a map, but the identification of the territory. Is the world we experience in all its details and chaos reality? That would say that we are not in contact with reality, and that our induced, abstracted information, our orderly symbolic systems, are all an artificial convenience. Perhaps this is wrong and the inverse is the case; true reality is in fact a system of deeper information, abstract ‘ideas’ at the root, which play out within this world we experience. If the latter is true, then the map we construct is an attempt to discover the inner informational truth out of which the world is birthed, and the world we see is merely a map, referencing the territory of a truer reality. This is the difference between Yisrael & Amim.

The inner spherical core of reality is chochmah, Torah. Beyond, we see an outer shell emanating from chochmah, our universe. Surrounding that outer shell is human sensory perception with which people try to make contact with the world. The 70 nations are on the outside, and try to induce, deduce and abduce reality with artificial self-generated systems that are always already doomed to be warped. Yisrael was handed an alien technology, a symbolic system that is magically able to express itself in earthly terms, and yet which has the keys for unlocking the inner core of reality.

During an oneg by R Ezra Neuberger, he told us all to draw the picture in this45 endnote our minds, and he described how to use this structure to understand the mivne of chumash Bereshit.

Torah, though it’s medaber kilshon bnei adam, is the symbolic system native to the core. Yisrael has access to truth from the top down, access to the alien technology that was not developed for convenience by the best guess of basar vadam but given from Kudsha Brich Hu. The goyim have no access, and must arrive at reality exclusively by the old modality of studying the map. So, the territory of the goyim is Alma like it was for all humanity kodem matan Torah, which is actually the map of Oraita. Yisrael has Oraita, through which they navigate Alma. During the Alpaim Tohu, the first 2,000 years until Avraham Avinu, access to reality was only through Alma, and Yisrael as we know it was scattered among the goyim with the hope that they’d independently look at alma and bring the world with them to Torah before Torah was given. The science of Alma was how the Avot, with the right kelim, were able to do just that even including the derabanans, because it’s not impossible in principle to navigate to the territory by studying the map. However, after the consolidation of Yisrael into a singular nation, beginning with Avraham Avinu, we initiate the Alpaim Torah. (Notice how Torah is the marriage document at Sinai between Kneset Yisrael and Kudsha Brich Hu, and it is the beginning of the ‘Torah” age begins not with Sinai but with the consolidation of Yisrael through Avaraham who was nivchar to be the Av of Yisrael). Now privileged access to reality shifts from Alma to Oraita directly. That is the magical object of chochmah which we are probing, the actual, singular root of an ‘Olam’ Echad.

There is a face that coheres from Shemotav HeKedoshim which is the Hu which we, the universe i.e. Shemo, have a relationship with. Those shemot are the Torah, which is just recombination’s of shemot, which is Him insofar as we are concerned. We never connect with Him BeAtzmuto, which is where we have the klal that no chochmah is about HaShem6. En Sof Baruch Hu is a bechina of Nivra, an interface, dual, not quite a Nivrah, but not quite Borei either. It is something called Elokut. Elokut is not our sugya; it is never a sugya, because our reality begins with His Ratzon, the Ohr En Sof, i.e., ‘Mah SheHaelokut Mitpashet.’

Adon Olam Asher Malach, Kudsha Brich Hu was king, but only after Yisrael, azai Hamelech Shemo nikra, He is called king. Why do we need this whole dynamic of being mamlich Kudsha Brich Hu? Is the fire department a hero if they are also the arsonist? For this we must return to the beginning, or in other words, the reshit, which is the rosh. The universe began with the Olam HaShaashuim, when Kudsha Brich Hu had the thought, “What would it be like to spend time with Yisrael?” and from that thought, He laughed a laugh of joy, and that motion, that na’anua, generated the entire Torah. The Torah is HaShem’s face in the universe, and it is His eye contact with the universe that makes it real, istakal beoraita ubara alma. But that’s not the point, the point is the generation of a second, an alterity, a Yisrael. The face of Yisrael is the face of the universe. The mechanism of the space in which Yisrael will individuate as an actual alterity is by self organizing without any intervention, becoming herself by herself, and going from dust to biology, from biology to consciousness, all in her own way, and finaly making space for a vayipach beapav, a breath which amounts to an initiation of dialogue with nukvah, and over time, that face matures and continues the dialogue. The face of the universe looks at Kudsha Brich Hu and says Hi, I’m Yisrael, I love you, and if I sometimes act in a way that doesn’t seem like that’s true, just remember, I’m made of stardust and it’s a miracle that stardust managed to speak at all! And this is why Yisrael, as the perception of the universe, is the soul of the universe, because it is Yisrael that can actually engage the function that this whole place was built for, a face to face conversation. Isn’t it the case that when Moshe, a bechinah of all Yisrael because he is a bechina of daat, he who speaks panim el panim with Kudsha Brich Hu, reports what he sees in conversation, that report is the Torah? So while Kudsha Brich Hu’s eye contact makes the universe real, our reciprocal, rebound eye contact makes His Malchut real. It is exclusively the middah of malchut that allows for this space to exist, because every other midah is just a fact and requires no relation to reify it. By contrast, Malchut is by definition a relational title, it is in reference to one who is the king of an am, which is why our people have a phrase (originally appearing in Rabeinu Bechaye, and its probably from an earlier medrash): En Melech Belo Am, there is no king without a nation. Now that we understand these things, you can understand why your entire avodah is not to perform things but to cultivate a relationship of Eye Contact with Kudsha Brich Hu, to look Him in the face and speak. This is what tefillah is supposed to be, this is why Torah is all about drishat Shemo, this is why emulating Kudsha Brich Hu in the context of chessed is really just an incarnation of vision, seeing the shape of His will in which you step to act when the situation calls you.

So that clarifies somewhat: we want Chochmah because we want to learn to see, and what we want to see is Him, and that desire is the engine driving us towards Chochmah in general, but this chochmah in particular will allow us to make contact with the actual territory rather than focusing on seeing the map more accurately. We don’t want to see the map, the map alienates us from the territory, because by staring at the map, we never actually feel natural and present in the territory of reality! But insofar as this world of Sod that we want to see is a particular form of Ratzon, a form that is territorial in relation to the cartographic reality of Olam HaZe Hagashmi, the world of Pshat, we need to develop our sense of the difference between these two layers of information. Our question becomes what Torah looks like in these different layers, and taking it slightly further, how might that change the kelim which we must bring for that Ohr?

Now our ears, primed with Ratzon, are ready to hear the material we find from Maharchu in the beginning of Shaar Kitvei Mori. He says that learning in the region of pshat is like the hazy memory of a dream which you have no tools to de-cipher7.

This is incredibly powerful if for nothing else than to frame the phenomenology8 of learning shat and how it must differ from learning sod. Phenomenology is a critical object to be familiar with as one progresses through the chochmah. It’s the experience of a specific section within a cluster of Being. While in reality an individual is composed of quite a large section of Being, the first-person, subjective consciousness of living within a body, embedded in material information, unable to access e.g. one’s makifim kolelim, unable to integrate the phenomenology of their animals and property within their field of view terminating at the surface of their skin. You own those objects, your shem is attatched to them, and thus they are a part of you, and yet you don’t know what it feels like to be your car, much less does your car’s experience of its nefesh domem continually insert feeling and experience in your mind! The phenomenology of being you is often identified with the pronoun I, the ‘self,’ but this is the reason why the havchana of phenomenal experience is so important in this chochmah: you are not your phenomenology. There is a critical error in expecting a phenomenological manifestation in all the things we do, the desire to feel a hormonal imprint of everything that goes on in shamayim or however you hope that mechanism might work. When you do a mitzvah of Torah or Tefillah, fire spills from your mouth, the olamot are euphorically energized, stadiums of Malachim cheer, and this happens with each word! The fact is, you don’t feel that, because those realities are real but phenomenologically unavailable. Just because it doesn’t enter into the slice of being that inputs data within your experience doesn’t mean that what you did doesn’t have an effect. This is obvious because our material sense systems and neurology are not windows through which that information ever comes through unless you specifically train for that, and for a long time! As enchanting as these pictures of mitzvot are, the symmetry is just as scary. For e.g., there are havalim that come from your ears, nose and mouth. When you listen to things you oughtn’t, there is a space in reality that is being abused and harassed, and you don’t feel it, because you’re experience neurologically only absorbs information presented in terms of neurology. And just as hearing is not a davar she’ein bo mamish, being that there are havalim yotze from the chalonot of oznayim, sight is the same. This goes beyond input, which we already know about; the real Ovdei HaShem concern themselves with output. Etz Chaim is masbir that like Achaf your eyes emit an Ohr of etzem enayim, and that can affect people. The gaze of Ra can make them lose their money while the rehabilitating gaze of hatava can cause healing and a sense of Other’s own greatness and beauty simply from the way you looked at them. A madregah of tikun yesod is learning how to gain control over these abilities, and with control, to rise in the potency of our engagement with the world. But will that always be phenomenologically experienced? No! These types of things enter into experience in ways that don’t have the force of blunt sensory stimulus, they don’t have the force some crackpot eastern drug tea, that is not how the world of reality operates. Growth as an Eved HaShem is a sober and earthly process, and the expectation of avodah as a bank to cash out your illusions of grandeur and dreams of astral experience will leave one feeling disappointed. ‘Feeling things’ will certainly occur through the process of this chochmah, but not in any way identifiable with the silly ideas people get in their head about the tzurah of ‘spirituality,’ itself a ridiculous word. Ruchniyut is if anything ethereality, more ‘air’ than afar, which reflects on the internal nature of the information insofar as Air is upstream of chumriyut. True avodah looks nothing like the glamour of editorially selective gadol maisim that spectacularize a flee from earthly experience. (There is a term in cybersecurity for the maze of login and authentication layers one has to go through to access a space on the internet, security theatre, which is called that because anybody who actually knows how the technology works sees how its just an orchestration of meaningless layers meant to give the feeling of security that don’t actually address digital vulnerability. But it’s not just that realm that engages in this sort of theatre, we are surrounded by theatre, by spectacular clothing that make us feel as though we are doing the thing when we are nowhere near the thing, but all the parts of the thing are there, look at my split hooves, but don’t look inside at my actual stomach, or look at my tears but don’t look at my actual thoughts. Kedusha theatre is sometimes a deception of the actor most of all.) The kavanot one learns in tefillah are at times decoupled from feeling on the level you would want because we aren’t always able to be mamshich mochin degadlut, and regardless, we always need to fight to get up for Shacharit. Phenomenology, though in essence a limitation, is also the window of reality’s disclosure during our career on earth. So, for example, when we are told that learning pshat is like a dream, we consider the experience of dreaming, compare it to when we are awake, and understand the relationship between dreaming, in its inaccess to reality and its jungle of twisted untruths, comparing that to the sobriety of wakefulness. Learning Sod should feel like waking up from a dream, in that when you wake up in the morning regardless of how cinematic your dreams were, the line that this is real and that wasn’t is undeniable. Unfortunately for some, sleep can mimic wakefulness when your phenomenology is embedded in dreamscape.

By this he tells us that the chochmah of pshat is an aspect of sleeping and forgetting, an attempt to recollect a memory of wakefulness, trying to reach back into the wakefulness of the womb before you were thrust in a world of sleep, a world of hazy dreams and un-reality; isn’t that the difference between wakefulness and sleep – to be in sober contact with actual Being exiling illusions concocted by lethally seductive blankets of darkness? And if reaching back to the wombstate is not in our past but towards our future, then it’s important to realize that although all Torah is the path en route to that same wombspace of wakeful clarity, the journey to wakeful vision is primarily through Sod and not Pshat; it’s important to realize, that is, only if the reclamation of childhood innocence and reentry into the glowing, blissful simplicity of pre-chet shining in all your sweetest memories and experiences is a goal you haven’t given up on through the bullying of Minim and Zedim, middle aged cynics and exiles from the Rachamim poured upon Tzadikim Vechasidim.

Maharchu also mentions that the relationship between the regions of pshat and sod is that of a Shifcha to an Isha, about which we know, the Eved is al menat lekabel pras and the Ben is shelo al menat lekabel pras. He writes that Chochmah in Atzilut is Sod, and when in Asiya it is called pshat. So apparently, what we are after is the Ohr Chochmah/Torah/Ratzon HaShem as manifested in a space called Atzilut, the world that issues from Chochmat Sod. Also, it would seem that relating to Kudsha Brich Hu on the level of Isha versus Shifcha is a path accessed through this region of chochmah davka, meaning one cannot be anything more than a Shifcha on the level Pshat alone. Needless to say, the experience of reality when one has internalized the perceptual paradigm of Isha versus Shifcha reveals a completely alien universe; in one world, you are a worker that is respected and valued but with little understanding of what goes on ‘upstairs’ (to use the Victorian designation for the family that owns the house, as opposed to the work staff who operate ‘downstairs’), while the other is an actual part of the family, with a seat at the table, on the inside.

  1. Virtual comes from the latin virtus meaning strength. Virtual is the antonym of Actual. Virtual means that it acts as if. You can replace the sun with a black hole of equal mass and it will have the same effect; it is virtually sun. The choreography of sensory data produced by digital media creates a virtual experience, where the person is not actually there, it’s a screen, but it generates an experience of the persons presence. Actual means reality. Many is not reality, but it is virtually real, just as atoms never touch each other, yet things are virtually solid; for all intents and purposes, solid.↩︎

  2. From the word Pashat, spread, as in the verb Poshet, sort of like the verb ma’atzil though without specific application to light…↩︎

  3. Gimel Rishonot, meaning the Kachab, refer to kelim of epistemology. Epistemology is a word denoting the apprehension of reality. In a world whose substance is information, we find that the information of Ohr is never variable but a function of the variation in the kli, in other words, Ani Havaya Lo Shaniti (Malachi 3:6). The generative question becomes how to shape those kelim to hold deeper alignment with reality as it is, so as to escape our own solipsistic distortions.↩︎

Also, as this is the first diagram I’ll mention that all of these were made by me unless otherwise specified, and done in MS Paint, or if I was feeling artistic/needed to indicate curvature and shading, in Sketchbook Pro. I don’t have any other tools besides for what comes with Microsoft, with the exception of Sketchbook Pro which I think is actually free, so forgive the muddiness and amateurish nature of the drawings. The accuracy of these diagrams is illustrative, but for example in the case of the otiot, not strictly accurate in terms of the number of nodes in each kav within the ot, which as it happens is not something I did any different than the original diagram I got it from which was made by a proper Chacham who gave a similar disclaimer. In any case, expect me to flag wherever there is an inaccuracy for the sake of artistic clarity. If you see anything that looks advanced, know now that it’s the bucket tool with a gradation setting and not actually any artistic skill on my part. [This was the original location of this note so I kept it in its place but as time has gone on, I have gotten a bit better at drawing. It remains the case that everything is drawn in Sketchbook Pro, and the aesthetics you see are a result of my inability to actually do art and so the tools that they have is as detailed as I can get. Layering textured paintbrushes and doing graded filling of spherical objects using their sphere ruler is responsible for most of what looks advanced. Many of the star patters are by using a symmetry line and drawing across the sections so that the intersection becomes a star. Some of the cuboid structures that have many parts were made by just copying one cube and joining it to the same layer and then copying that etc. such that I have a massive cube of exponentially smaller cubes. Also, they have a text tool but it’s not a word processor so I need to make all the paragraphs and sizing myself which is what accounts for the awkward placement that eventually became a stylistic tool I used to emphasize and lead the eye through the information I wanted to write about. They have a color wheel that always shows the complimentary color which is basically the opposite side of whatever color you’re on, so that’s usually my go to choice for contrast. My point in showing how the sausage is made here is that it’s really not that difficult to adopt this diagrammatic style if it is usefull to you, and also as an excuse for the sketchiness of the drawings that might be misinterpreted as a lack of respect for the reader that deserves to have more clarity in presentation. The main thing I’d say I learned is that just like vocabulary, if there is a thought you need to get out, you will of necessity find the right words to hold the texture of your thought. Similarly, there is an image and I am forced to develop a visual language to share it with you. So, if you think in terms of diagrams and visuals, keep drawing and writing, and eventually you will find a visual grammar that dresses your thought.]↩︎

  6. This nekudah is something we will reinforce at exhaustive length in the third piece. It’s also the point that provides most people with their excuse to withhold from the limud. It’s a valid concern, but even for us, we will go through the sugya, hopefully come to an understanding, and it wont be the last we see of it because the sefarim are also paranoid on exactly this same nekudah and will foist on you, for good reason, these clarifications wherever possible. But this level of concern is unfounded when we already liven a cerebral landscape that does the heavy lifting for us. This is the shitah of R Mechel Handler, that in our generation we are so used to abstraction, there is less of a need to go on and on with the harchakas from hitgashmut, though to be fair the point of distinguishing between Ohr En Sof and Shemot and En Sof is something that needs more care. This distinction remains one that forms the scope and aim of chochmah notwithstanding our ease with abstraction.↩︎
